prerequisites: Successful completion of the first year of study in the Master's program
Fundamentals of project management and scientific work

learning_outcomes.text: Students apply scientific methods and work techniques within a limited application project with research relevance. They also master project management techniques.
Students possess expanded and deepened knowledge regarding a selected topic area and the necessary engineering methods. The topic area is determined by the choice of the problem to be addressed.

Students formulate research questions, identify and analyze relevant literature and data for the project. They critically question existing solutions and concepts and evaluate the effectiveness and impact of the solutions.

Students analyze a previously unknown, complex problem and, based on this, write a requirements specification or work plan. They design a time and milestone plan for a project. They independently find and evaluate solutions or solution approaches for a previously unknown, complex problem in a team/group within a given time. They apply known and new methods/tools for problem-solving.

Students derive new concepts from known solutions by formulating hypotheses. They implement the found solutions and optimize them during the course of the project. They interpret the results in relation to the task.

Students document self-developed solutions and solution approaches for a target group and discuss concepts and solution drafts with relevant stakeholders. They communicate with clients in a goal-oriented and target-group-appropriate manner. They work effectively in teams and present developed solutions and solution approaches to a specialist audience and the client. They can assess their role in a team and take responsibility in a team.

Students utilize mechanisms of scientific information retrieval. They critically reflect on information in new knowledge areas. They evaluate new methods/tools for problem-solving and develop them for themselves.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of the task and definition of goals
Creation of a timetable or milestone plan
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance consists of a written project report. In addition to a written report, the results are presented in a presentation. The project report should be 10 - 30 pages per examinee.
